title: Compatibility telemetry and migration orchestrator for fallback variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Smart routing selects region/tier and fallback model variants under load or failure. Recent incidents show silent regressions when fallback variants differ in tokenizer, KV cache behavior, or structured-output tooling. Maintaining an accurate compatibility matrix is brittle when done manually.

Goal: Build a low-latency telemetry pipeline and a migration orchestrator that detect tokenizer/context/tooling parity drift between primary and fallback variants, create rollback-safe migration plans, and automate routine compatibility validations as part of rollout. This reduces incidents, speeds safe rollouts, and ensures routing fallbacks preserve output quality and tooling expectations.

Proposed approach:
1) Compatibility telemetry: instrument serving runtime to emit compact compatibility vectors per model variant (tokenizer hash/version, max_context, kv-cache-semantics tag, special-token map checksum, quantization profile id, supported-kernel-features). Aggregate these to a time-series store and correlate with anomalies in outputs (e.g., tokenization splits, truncated sequences, reranking score drift).

2) Drift detection and alerts: define deterministic checks and ML-based change detectors that fire when variant pairs diverge on critical fields or when downstream eval metrics degrade after a routing event. Expose alerts in Console with link to failing request examples.

3) Migration orchestrator: a service that can run staged compatibility checks during a rollout: synthetic prompt suites, in-situ A/B parity runs (sampled traffic with sidecars), and automated remediation steps (disable fallback, pin variant, or run auto-sanitization transforms like tokenizer normalization). Provide a manual override in Console and integrate with rollout policies (canary/abort thresholds).

4) Tooling & CI: add pre-deploy compatibility tests to model onboarding pipelines (GitHub Actions), include tokenizer/context contract checks in preflight, and generate per-variant compatibility manifests stored with the model artifact.

5) Documentation & runbook: ship a concise runbook for on-call and SRE describing detection, diagnosis, remediation, and how to use the orchestrator to roll back or migrate variants.

Artifacts/links:
- Confluence draft (design): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compatibility+Telemetry+Design
- Proto dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/compatibility/variant-metrics
- Draft PR for telemetry proto and runtime hook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4392
- Onboarding checklist proposal: https://docs.redwood.ai/model-onboarding/compatibility-checks

Risks & constraints:
- Telemetry overhead must be sub-millisecond for high QPS variants; design must compress fields and sample intelligently.
- False positives from tokenization sensitivity across language locales — need curated prompt suites per language.
- Rollout orchestration must be non-blocking for emergency hotfixes and support immediate manual aborts.

Next steps:
- Week 1: finalize telemetry schema, land minimal runtime hook (PR 4392), and prototype Grafana panels.
- Week 2: implement simple drift rules, wire alerts into Console, and author runbook.
- Week 3: add orchestrator service skeleton, and run first in-situ parity run against two internal fallback variants.
- Week 4: iterate on false-positive tuning and add CI preflight checks to model onboarding pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema landed and runtime emits compatibility vectors for all active variants at sampling rate <= 0.1% with <0.5ms p95 overhead
Dashboard shows per-variant tokenizer/hash/context metrics and ability to filter by region and tier
Drift rule implementation triggers test alerts for synthetic divergence scenarios
Orchestrator can execute a staged parity run (synthetic suite + sampled sidecar) and produce a compatibility report
Preflight CI checks fail when tokenizer/context contracts are violated and block model promotion
